quality_guards: Scarlet-fever risk depends on case timing, contact patterns, setting, hygiene, vulnerability, treatment and outbreak response.
Hepatitis-A risk depends on immunity, exposure route, hygiene, contact timing, food handling, vulnerability and prophylaxis.
Hepatitis-E risk depends on viral strain, food source, cooking, cross-contamination, immunity, pregnancy and clinical status.
Cryptosporidium risk depends on water treatment, animal contact, hygiene, exposure dose, immunity, setting and outbreak controls.
Giardiasis risk depends on water quality, sanitation, travel, contact patterns, hygiene, exposure dose and host factors.
Reservoir risk depends on dam condition, storage, hydrology, inspection, maintenance, downstream exposure and emergency planning.
HGV walkaround risk depends on vehicle configuration, load, defect condition, maintenance, route, weather and driver competence.
Heavy-vehicle brake risk depends on system design, load, adjustment, wear, maintenance, test method and operating conditions.
Red-X risk depends on incident location, traffic flow, visibility, compliance, emergency access and road-operating conditions.
Notification value depends on clinical suspicion, reporting timeliness, diagnostic completeness, case definition and follow-up.
Scarlet-fever evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, treatment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Hepatitis-A evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, vaccination- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Hepatitis-E evidence is food-, exposure-, person-, clinical- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Cryptosporidium evidence is source-, water-, exposure-, person- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Giardia evidence is source-, travel-, water-, person- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Reservoir evidence is asset-, catchment-, engineering-, downstream- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level flood probability.
HGV-check evidence is vehicle-, defect-, journey-, operator- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
Brake-test evidence is vehicle-, axle-, load-, maintenance- and test-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
Red-X evidence is motorway-, lane-, incident-, driver- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level casualty probability.
NOIDs evidence is report-, disease-, laboratory-, jurisdiction- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
